# Island

A floating pill that changes with what the viewer is doing. Each state is a view, and switching views morphs the pill to its new size while the contents crossfade in place.

```tsx
const pane = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
const progress = useScrollProgress(pane) // no argument: the document
const scrolled = progress > 3

<Island aria-label="Journal" view={post ? "reading" : "browse"}>
  <IslandView value="browse">
    <IslandButton tooltip="Dark theme" shortcut="L" onClick={toggleTheme}>
      <Moon weight="bold" />
    </IslandButton>
    <IslandButton tooltip="Layout grid" shortcut="G" pressed={grid} onClick={toggleGrid}>
      <GridFour weight="bold" />
    </IslandButton>
    <IslandSeparator />
    <LanguageMenu />
  </IslandView>

  <IslandView value="reading">
    <IslandButton tooltip="Back to journal" onClick={back}>
      <ArrowLeft weight="bold" />
    </IslandButton>
    <IslandSwap view={scrolled ? "top" : undefined}>
      <IslandView value="top">
        <IslandButton tooltip="Back to top" onClick={scrollToTop}>
          <ArrowUp weight="bold" />
        </IslandButton>
      </IslandView>
    </IslandSwap>
    <IslandButton tooltip="Save for later" pressed={saved} onClick={toggleSaved}>
      <BookmarkSimple weight={saved ? "fill" : "bold"} />
    </IslandButton>
    <IslandSeparator />
    <IslandSwap view={scrolled ? "progress" : "title"}>
      <IslandView value="title">
        <IslandTitle>{post.title}</IslandTitle>
      </IslandView>
      <IslandView value="progress">
        <IslandProgress value={progress} transition="none" aria-label="Reading progress" />
      </IslandView>
    </IslandSwap>
  </IslandView>
</Island>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add island
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/island/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import {
  Island,
  IslandView,
  IslandSwap,
  IslandButton,
  IslandIcon,
  IslandSeparator,
  IslandTitle,
  IslandProgress,
} from "@/components/ui/island"

<Island
  aria-label="Page"
  view={reading ? "reading" : "browse"}
  className="fixed bottom-6 left-1/2 z-50 -translate-x-1/2"
>
  <IslandView value="browse">
    <IslandButton tooltip="Dark theme" shortcut="L">
      <Moon weight="bold" />
    </IslandButton>
  </IslandView>
  <IslandView value="reading">
    <IslandButton tooltip="Back">
      <ArrowLeft weight="bold" />
    </IslandButton>
    <IslandSeparator />
    <IslandTitle>{post.title}</IslandTitle>
  </IslandView>
</Island>
```

Mount it once, in the layout, and drive `view` from the route. An island that each page renders for itself is a new island on every navigation, so it can only appear, never morph. Pin it yourself, the way you would any floating surface: fixed and centred, so it grows out from its middle, above `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` on a phone.

## Variants

Floating is the default: the elevated popover surface, with the controls resting muted until one of them holds a state. Solid is the inverted slab, the closest thing to the hardware island and the one to reach for over a photograph, a video or a canvas. It flips foreground and background instead of hardcoding black, so it stays legible in all four themes.

```tsx
{/* floating (default) */}
<Island aria-label="Page">…</Island>

{/* solid */}
<Island aria-label="Page" variant="solid">…</Island>
```

## Sizes

`size` is the island's own density axis, not the page's comfortable/compact knob: a floating control bar that shrinks to form-compact becomes hard to hit. `md` is the original's 44px pill and `lg` the touch step. At every size, padding plus half a control is half the pill, so the round controls sit concentric in its ends.

```tsx
<Island size="sm">…</Island>
<Island size="md">…</Island>  {/* default */}
<Island size="lg">…</Island>
```

## Views

Declare every state as an `IslandView` and name the one on screen with `view`. Only that view is mounted, plus, for one beat, the one leaving. The pill eases to the new width and height while the old contents blur out and the new ones blur in. A view is a row; give it `flex-col` and the pill grows into a card, its corner easing from half the height to the card's radius on the same clock. `IslandIcon` holds a status glyph at a control's size, and `IslandProgress` is the readout and bar for a task that is running.

```tsx
<Island aria-label="Publish" view={view}>
  <IslandView value="idle">
    <IslandButton tooltip="Preview"><Eye weight="bold" /></IslandButton>
    <IslandButton tooltip="History"><ClockCounterClockwise weight="bold" /></IslandButton>
    <IslandSeparator />
    <Button onClick={publish}>Publish</Button>
  </IslandView>

  <IslandView value="publishing">
    <IslandIcon>
      <Spinner aria-hidden />
    </IslandIcon>
    <IslandTitle className="pl-0">Publishing</IslandTitle>
    <IslandProgress value={progress} aria-label="Publishing" />
  </IslandView>

  {/* flex-col: the pill grows into a card */}
  <IslandView value="published" className="w-72 flex-col items-stretch gap-1.5 p-2.5">
    <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-3 pl-3">
      <p className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm font-medium">
        <CheckCircle weight="fill" className="size-4 text-success" />
        Published
      </p>
      <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" className="text-muted-foreground" onClick={undo}>
        Undo
      </Button>
    </div>
    {/* The address is the way in: no second "Visit" button repeating it. */}
    <Button asChild variant="secondary" className="justify-between">
      <a href={url} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">
        <Globe weight="bold" className="text-muted-foreground" />
        <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate">koala-journal.vercel.app</span>
        <ArrowUpRight weight="bold" className="text-muted-foreground" />
      </a>
    </Button>
  </IslandView>
</Island>
```

## Swap

`IslandSwap` is a region of a view that changes on its own, with the same crossfade and a small morph of its own: the title that gives way to the progress readout once you scroll. Name a view no child answers to and the region empties and collapses to nothing, which is how a “back to top” grows into the pill past the fold and out of it again at the top.

```tsx
<IslandSwap view={scrolled ? "top" : undefined}>
  <IslandView value="top">
    <IslandButton tooltip="Back to top"><ArrowUp weight="bold" /></IslandButton>
  </IslandView>
</IslandSwap>
<IslandSeparator />
<IslandSwap view={scrolled ? "progress" : "title"}>
  <IslandView value="title">
    <IslandTitle>Three durations are enough</IslandTitle>
  </IslandView>
  <IslandView value="progress">
    <IslandProgress value={42} aria-label="Reading progress" />
  </IslandView>
</IslandSwap>
```

## Buttons and menus

One glyph makes an `IslandButton` a circle, a word makes it a pill. `pressed` lights the chip for a toggle that is on, `shortcut` puts a keycap in the tooltip, and `caret` turns it into a menu trigger whose caret points at the menu while it is open. Open menus upward, away from the edge the island sits on, and keep the Tooltip outside the trigger so the menu keeps its own hold on the button.

```tsx
<IslandButton tooltip="Dark theme" shortcut="L"><Moon weight="bold" /></IslandButton>
<IslandButton tooltip="Layout grid" shortcut="G" pressed><GridFour weight="bold" /></IslandButton>
<IslandButton tooltip="Comments are off on this page" disabled><ChatCircle weight="bold" /></IslandButton>
<IslandSeparator />
<IslandButton><ShareNetwork weight="bold" />Share</IslandButton>

<DropdownMenu>
  <Tooltip content="Language" placement="top">
    <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
      <IslandButton caret aria-label="Language: English">
        <Flag />
        <span>EN</span>
      </IslandButton>
    </DropdownMenuTrigger>
  </Tooltip>
  <DropdownMenuContent side="top" align="end">…</DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

## API reference

### Island

The morphing pill and the roving-focus root (Radix `Toolbar.Root`, so it forwards `dir`, `loop` and the rest). Takes `view` (the value of the view on screen), `variant` (floating · solid), `size` (sm · md · lg) and `tooltipPlacement` (default `"top"`). Without views, its children are simply its contents, and it still eases when they change size.

### IslandView

One state, named by `value`. Mounted while it is on screen; while it leaves it is out of flow, `inert` and hidden from assistive tech. A row by default; `className` can make it a card.

### IslandSwap

A region inside a view with its own `view` and its own `IslandView` children. A value no child answers to collapses it to nothing.

### IslandButton

A control (Radix `Toolbar.Button`). Takes `tooltip` (a string also becomes its `aria-label`), `shortcut`, `pressed`, `caret`, `disabled` and `asChild`.

### IslandIcon · IslandTitle · IslandProgress · IslandSeparator

`IslandIcon` is a status glyph at a control's size. `IslandTitle` is one line that truncates before it stretches the pill. `IslandProgress` takes `value` (0 to 100, or `null` for an unknown length), `transition` and an `aria-label`; its bar is our Progress. `IslandSeparator` is the hairline between clusters.

## FAQ

### How is this different from Dock and Toolbar?

Toolbar is a band of controls that keeps one shape. Dock is navigation that changes shape on demand: a rail you expand into a labelled menu. Island changes with context rather than on demand: its views follow what the viewer is doing (browsing, reading, waiting on a task), and it swaps them in place. All three sit on Radix Toolbar, so they share the roving focus and the arrow keys.

### Why declare every view up front instead of rendering the one I need?

Because the island has to keep the old view for one beat while it blurs out. With every view declared, the one leaving is the same instance that was on screen a moment ago, with its state and its tooltips, rather than a snapshot re-rendered in its place. Views that are neither on screen nor leaving are not mounted, so declaring them costs nothing.

### Where does it get its size?

From its own contents. The pill measures an inner viewport that is free to be its natural size, so mid-change it already knows where it is going, and CSS tweens the width, height and corner to it. The corner is half the height while the island is one row, capped at the card radius once a view grows taller, so one formula covers the pill and the card.

### Why should it live in the layout?

So it survives navigation. Driven by the route from the layout, going from a list to a post is a view change and the pill morphs. Rendered by each page, it would unmount with the old page and mount with the new one, and a new element can only appear.

### How do I show reading progress?

Pass useScrollProgress() (from Progress) to IslandProgress with transition="none", so the bar is welded to the scrollbar instead of trailing it. With no argument it reads the document; pass a ref to follow a scroll container instead. Swap the title for it with an IslandSwap once the reader has scrolled a little.

### What happens to focus when a view changes?

If the control you pressed lives in the view that is leaving (a Back button, say), focus moves to the first control still on screen, so a keyboard user is never dropped onto the page. The leaving view is inert while it fades, so nothing in it can be tabbed to or read out.

### Does it respect reduced motion?

Yes. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the pill resizes instantly, the old view goes without waiting for a fade and the new one does not animate in. Every functional state (pressed chips, the open menu, focus rings) stays exactly as it is.

### Does it follow the page's comfortable/compact density?

No, by design, the same call as Dock and Toolbar. Its size axis (sm / md / lg) is its own density knob, because a floating control bar that shrinks to form-compact becomes hard to hit. Use lg where the island is mostly touched.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add island` writes `components/ui/island/`. Import from `@/components/ui/island`:

- Components and helpers: `Island`, `IslandView`, `IslandSwap`, `IslandButton`, `IslandIcon`, `IslandSeparator`, `IslandTitle`, `IslandProgress`, `islandVariants`
- Types: `IslandProps`, `IslandViewProps`, `IslandSwapProps`, `IslandButtonProps`, `IslandIconProps`, `IslandTitleProps`, `IslandProgressProps`
- Koala components it installs with it: `kbd`, `progress`, `tooltip`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `create-context`, `hit-area`, `morph`, `motion`, `tv`
- npm packages: `@phosphor-icons/react`, `radix-ui`
